The problem

VTU has 3.5 lakh students across 219 colleges.
Placements happened informally, inequitably, and invisibly.

Engineering colleges affiliated to VTU — one of India's largest technical universities — had no central placement system. Each college ran its own process: spreadsheets, WhatsApp groups, emails, physical notice boards. Students from tier-2 and tier-3 cities were effectively invisible to recruiters who concentrated on Bengaluru campuses.

Companies had no way to access verified student profiles across the university. TPOs (Training and Placement Officers) had no central view of which students applied where, who got shortlisted, or where their cohort stood against industry requirements. The problem wasn't a lack of talent — it was a lack of infrastructure.

The brief: Design a unified placement platform — Xcelerator — that serves three completely different user types (students, TPOs, industry partners) from a single system, without making anyone feel like they're using someone else's tool.

This was a greenfield B2C/B2B hybrid product with real users, real institutional partners, and a launch deadline tied to VTU events across four cities in January 2025. The Times of India covered the launch.

User interviews across all three personas
Three users, one system

The core design challenge wasn't any single portal — it was making sure three completely different users felt the platform was built for them. Each had distinct goals, different levels of digital literacy, and conflicting definitions of what "good" looked like.

What research told us

50+ interviews across all three user groups. We went into placements offices, spoke to final-year students who'd been through placement cycles, and interviewed recruiters about where their current process broke down.

01
Students from non-Bengaluru colleges felt the system wasn't for them

Tier-2 college students consistently said recruiters "don't come here." Remote opportunities existed — they just didn't know where to find them or whether their profiles would be taken seriously. This shaped how we framed the student landing page: leading with geographical access, not just job listings.

02
TPOs were drowning in administrative coordination, not strategic placement

Most TPOs maintained Excel sheets for tracking student statuses, sent individual emails to companies, and had no visibility into what competing colleges were doing. The biggest ask: a single view of their entire cohort with completion status. Not analytics — just visibility.

03
Recruiters didn't trust unverified student data

Multiple company representatives said they'd ignore platforms where students self-reported skills with no validation. This informed our decision to prominently surface "Verified" and "219+ Colleges" in the industry portal — trust signals up front, not buried in FAQs.

04
Students didn't know what "job ready" meant in practice

When asked whether they were ready for a specific job, most students said "I think so" or "I don't know." This insight directly led to the Readiness Estimator — a tool to make job readiness legible and actionable, not just a vague feeling.

The product
Portal 01

Student — Xcelerate towards your dream career

For students across 219 VTU colleges. Prepare, apply, succeed.

Student portal — desktop
Prepare → Apply → Succeed
Three-step mental model anchors the landing page. Not feature-led — outcome-led. Students understand the journey before they sign in.
Resume Builder
Guided ATS-compatible resume creation. Students without design experience produce recruiter-ready CVs without knowing what ATS means.
AI Interview Guide
Mock interviews with AI feedback. Addresses the most common student anxiety: not knowing what to expect in an actual interview.
Readiness Estimator
Gap analysis against specific job requirements. Turns "I think I'm ready" into a concrete list of what needs work.
Live job board + Hackathons
Samsung, Wipro, HCL — 50+ companies actively recruiting. Industry events and hackathons surfaced on the landing page, not buried inside the app.
Portal 02

College — Xcelerate your placement drive

For TPOs at 219 affiliated colleges. Manage, track, and close gaps.

College (TPO) portal — desktop
Onboard students & showcase talent
Aggregate and share student profiles with companies. What used to require individual emails is now a filtered export.
Central placement drive view
All ongoing placement drives, their status, gaps, and student participation — visible from one dashboard. TPOs stop chasing updates.
Skill gap analysis
Identify which students are ready for which roles. Run targeted preparation before companies arrive, not after rejections come in.
Video tutorials embedded at launch
TPOs had varying digital literacy. Onboarding videos for every key action were embedded directly in the landing page — reducing support load from day one.
Portal 03

Industry — Xcelerate towards optimised hiring

For 500+ companies. Post jobs, find matching candidates, hire.

Industry portal — desktop
Trust signals lead, not features
3.5L+ verified students. 219 colleges. 10+ graduation streams. 50+ locations. These live above the fold — because recruiters needed to believe the pool was real before reading anything else.
Filtered candidate access
Skills, performance, stream, location. Recruiters access detailed profiles and CVs directly — no intermediary, no back-and-forth with individual TPOs.
Placement pipeline management
Track applicants stage by stage. Promote, shortlist, send offers — from one dashboard across all participating colleges simultaneously.
Tier-2 & Tier-3 reach by design
Remote opportunities, hackathons, and college-agnostic filtering let companies access talent they'd previously written off as inaccessible. This was a key differentiator from existing job portals.
Portal 04

Mobile — all three portals, responsive

Student, College, and Industry portals fully responsive. Designed at 375px and 428px breakpoints.

Navigation
Hamburger menu with full-screen overlay

All four nav links visible on open. Sign In stays persistent. The mobile nav is the same on all three portals — one mental model regardless of which entry point the user came from.

Student mobile
Prepare → Apply → Succeed stays intact

The three-step mental model from desktop translates directly to mobile. Job cards stack vertically. Hackathon events are full-bleed cards with imagery — more browsable on mobile than on desktop.

College mobile
Feature sections collapse gracefully

The alternating image/text layout from desktop stacks to vertical on mobile. Each feature section leads with the heading, then the supporting visual, so the scanning hierarchy stays intact.

Industry mobile
Trust metrics still above the fold

3.5L+ students, 219 colleges — the four key stats remain above the fold on mobile. Post a Job CTA stays sticky in context. The value proposition is legible before any scrolling.

Portal map & user flows

Before screens, we mapped every user's core job-to-be-done and the sequence of actions required to complete it — across all three portals. This is what drove feature prioritisation and informed where portals needed to talk to each other.

Portal map: student, TPO, and industry user flows — Figma, 2024
Key design decisions
Decision 01 — Information architecture
"Should the three portals share navigation or be completely separate experiences?"

Completely separate — but with a shared nav bar that links between them. Each portal has its own distinct hero, value proposition, and primary CTA. A student landing on the college portal should feel like they're in the wrong place. That friction is intentional — it keeps each experience focused on one user type's goals.

Decision 02 — Industry portal
"Where do trust signals go — hero or further down the page?"

Hero, without hesitation. Research showed that recruiters who landed on a placement platform and didn't immediately see scale numbers left quickly. 3.5L+ verified students and 219 colleges need to be the first thing a recruiter reads. Features come second. Credibility comes first.

Decision 03 — Student tools
"How do you explain AI Interview Guide and Readiness Estimator to students who've never seen either?"

Name the outcome, not the mechanism. "Engage in mock interviews and get AI-driven feedback" is clearer than explaining what AI means in this context. The student tools section leads with what you get, not how it works. Video tutorials handle the how.

Decision 04 — Onboarding
"TPOs have varying digital literacy — how do you onboard them without a training programme?"

Embed video tutorials directly in the landing page for each key action. Not a help centre link, not a separate onboarding flow — contextual videos next to each feature description. The landing page is also the training material. This was validated by the CPC Director in the launch testimonial.

What I learned
01
Designing for three user types in one system is a trust problem, not a feature problem

The temptation is to solve multi-user platforms by adding features for each user. The actual work is making each user feel the platform was built for them specifically. That's done through language, hierarchy, and what's placed above the fold — not through feature parity.

02
Research with institutional users is different from research with consumers

Interviewing TPOs in placement offices — not in a UX lab, not over a Zoom call — surfaced things that surveys never would. The spreadsheet problem, the WhatsApp coordination, the anxiety about companies "not coming to us." Getting into their environment changed what we built.

03
A launch deadline tied to physical events is a different kind of pressure

Four city events in January 2025 meant the platform had to be credible enough to demo to TPOs and VTU officials in person. That changes prioritisation completely — certain rough edges that might survive a soft digital launch cannot survive a room full of placement officers seeing it for the first time.

04
Scale numbers are part of the UX, not just the marketing

3.5L students, 219 colleges, 500+ companies — these aren't just marketing stats. For a student from Kalaburagi wondering if this platform is relevant to them, seeing those numbers is what keeps them on the page. Data as trust design.
